baseline.$comment: RFC-0018 CO-4: the rung's serving record served at the ladder's concurrencies; full load is the lowest concurrency within the plateau of the highest rate. Null fields and a cause when no baseline run is stored or none of its ladder rungs succeeded.

gpu_model.$comment: CO-8 (amended 2026-11-16): the GPU model the serving run's manifest records (machine.gpu.model); null with no baseline; optional, added in place (Q14 precedent)

reply_tokens_per_gpu_second.$comment: CO-8 (amended 2026-11-16): the request's reply tokens over the baseline's GPU-seconds per reply at full load, unit token/gpu_s, the baseline's scope; one rate over one run's timed batches, no range; over a row's session_reply_tokens_per_gpu_second it is the row's session_multiple; optional, added in place (Q14 precedent)

check.$comment: RFC-0018 §The six checks: an undecided check names its cause; held and failed name none. `note` carries a publisher's sentence (CH-5) or the harness's reason.

trials.$comment: RFC-0018 CH-1c: per control and position, the counted trials, how many were refused, how many of those by the prover making no proof (no_proof, a declared P1 stop, CH-1a), and how many distinct changed inputs they sent (MODEL, PROMPT, REPLY)

formal.$comment: Machine-checked's facts copied from properties/2 (RFC-0018 MC-1 to MC-6): the step the publisher's words reach before the proof build lowers it, and the scope card; build, present when a proof-build record is stored, is that record as the system page prints it (RFC-0018 GL-5, amended 2026-11-16)

command.$comment: what ran, without our time-limit wrapper: the publisher's command with its settings

axioms.$comment: the axioms the build reports for the theorem, sorted (amended 2026-11-17); printed with the record

conclusion.$comment: MC-7 (amended 2026-11-15): what the theorem's conclusion is about, from properties/2

ceiling.$comment: MC-7 (amended 2026-11-15): the most a matching proof build can give, the stated step lowered by MC-7; never above the stated step

scope_bounds.$comment: the publisher's bound for each scope-card row, verbatim with its quotes, or null; printed, sets no state

said.$comment: each fact's quotes and plain words, by fact, as the page prints them (amended 2026-11-17); it sets nothing

limits.$comment: the limits the publisher states that no rule reads, each in plain words with its quotes (amended 2026-11-17); printed, they set nothing

petal.$comment: RFC-0018 §The glyph: one petal. `step` is the decided step, a word (GL-8); `state` is its ink, derived from the step; `cause` says why a petal is red or hollow; `basis` says whether the publisher's documents or our checks decided it; `lowered_by` names the checks that set it red (GL-2). The row's prefixItems fix each id.

allOf.$comment: state is the step's ink; a green or amber petal has no cause
GL-3: a hollow petal is not decided and names why
GL-2: a petal our check set red names the checks; no other petal names any
only Machine-checked carries `formal`; null when its properties file is not read
only Weights hidden carries `visible`; null when its properties file is not read

reading.$comment: N1: true when a fact the petal's decision read carries a note, so the value is the reader's reading, not the publisher's words; absent means false

next.$comment: RFC-0018 GL-11 (adopted 2026-11-16): the petal's next step, computed on the path that sets its step: the step it would move to (null on a hollow petal, what decides it; or on a failed one, its repair) and each need with who acts; null at green. It sets nothing and is never summed or sorted (GL-8). Optional, added in place (Q14 precedent)

sources_read.$comment: R-SILENT: on a red with cause not_stated, the documents read, each linked at the pin; absent otherwise

forms.$comment: Weights hidden: the forms of the proved zero knowledge, the publisher's words with their quotes (properties/2 hiding.forms); printed, sets no step

visible_at_least.$comment: Weights hidden: true when the publisher says its list of visible values is a lower bound

notes.$comment: RFC-0018 GL-10 (amended 2026-11-15): with reading true, the notes of the facts the decision read, our reading in words, printed with the petal

to_met.$comment: RFC-0018 GL-11 (amended 2026-11-17): everything the row lacks for Met, computed on the path that sets the step, in groups by the step each group reaches (`to`; null and `kind` decide or repair on a hollow or failed petal), each item a key the site words (`need`), who acts (`by`) and the numbers and names it is worded with; `text` items carry the next step's own words. Empty at Met. It sets nothing and is never summed or sorted (GL-8)

sources.$comment: GL-5 (amended 2026-11-17): what the step comes from, printed beside it: our test, the publisher's words, our rebuild of its theorem, and our reading; null on a Not stated or Not decided petal

sources_count.$comment: the number of `read_facts` the step read (`used`), printed with a reading; no state reads it

read_facts.$comment: GL-10 (amended 2026-11-17): the facts with a note that the step or a need for Met rests on, each with the reviewer's note and its plain words (`plain`, from the properties file, or null)

used.$comment: whether the decision that set the step read the fact (N1); false: only Met's rule reads it, and Met needs the publisher's words in its place (GL-11, amended 2026-11-17)

why.$comment: the inputs of the system page's Why line on UF-9, WH-6 and MC-6 (amended 2026-11-17); no state reads them

bound.$comment: Integrity's facts as the system page words them (amended 2026-11-17), copied from the properties file or the stored fidelity record with values computed from them (thresholds and means to one decimal, `q_cross`, `below_own_width`, `policy_cap`, `clause`); no state reads them

hiding.$comment: Confidentiality's facts as the system page words them (amended 2026-11-17), copied from the properties file or the stored fidelity record with values computed from them (thresholds and means to one decimal, `q_cross`, `below_own_width`, `policy_cap`, `clause`); no state reads them

fidelity.$comment: Fidelity's facts as the system page words them (amended 2026-11-17), copied from the properties file or the stored fidelity record with values computed from them (thresholds and means to one decimal, `q_cross`, `below_own_width`, `policy_cap`, `clause`); no state reads them

trust.$comment: Trust assumptions's facts as the system page words them (amended 2026-11-17), copied from the properties file or the stored fidelity record with values computed from them (thresholds and means to one decimal, `q_cross`, `below_own_width`, `policy_cap`, `clause`); no state reads them

allOf.$comment: OR-1, OR-4: only a passed, ranked row holds a position

generation_multiple.$comment: CO-7: the generation part over the baseline's GPU-seconds per reply

glyph.$comment: GL-1 to GL-9: the five petals in drawing order; no field sums, counts or orders them (GL-8); never moves a position (GL-4)

incomplete_sessions.$comment: SE-3: a session that ended incomplete, with its exit code and cause (AGENTS.md rule 5); it enters no figure and no check except RUN

ineligible_sessions.$comment: RFC-0018 SE-3b: a run RFC-0014 §Eligibility keeps out of the release, with its reason codes; it enters no figure and no check, RUN's attempts included

level_statement.$comment: RFC-0018 SI-4a: the publisher's statement, recorded at the pin in the properties file, that an accept means the reply is the committed model's own computation, decoded greedily, on the prompt. A passed row without it takes no position.

multiple.$comment: CO-5: mean steady m over the baseline's GPU-seconds per reply; null (not_applicable) when the row has no steady state

proving_multiple.$comment: CO-7: the proving part over the baseline's GPU-seconds per reply

replaced_sessions.$comment: SE-3a: a counted session whose verify ran with a GPU visible and whose proofs were not kept, replaced in its slot by a later session of the same pin; it enters no figure and no check

session_commit_and_proving_gpu_seconds_p.$comment: CO-7 (amended 2026-11-13): the session cost per reply less its generation part (commit, the prove call outside its generation phase and the seconds between the two calls), mean of the counted sessions, scope whole_wall; null when the system has no generation phase of its own

session_commit_gpu_seconds_per_reply.$comment: CO-7 (amended 2026-11-15): the commit call's GPU-seconds (commit.start to commit.end) over N, mean of the counted sessions, scope commit

session_proving_gpu_seconds_per_reply.$comment: CO-7 (amended 2026-11-15): the session cost per reply less its commit part and its generation part (zero with no generation phase of its own), mean of the counted sessions, scope whole_wall

generation_gpu_seconds_per_reply_token.$comment: CO-7 (amended 2026-11-15): the generation phase's GPU-seconds per reply over the request's reply tokens, mean of the counted sessions; null when the system has no generation phase of its own

session_reply_tokens_per_gpu_second.$comment: CO-8 (adopted 2026-11-16): the request's reply tokens over the mean of the counted sessions' GPU-seconds per reply (CO-1), scope whole_wall, unit token/gpu_s; its range the tokens over the largest and the smallest session; printed once, on the system page under Cost; optional, added in place (Q14 precedent)

session_commit_and_proving_multiple.$comment: CO-7 (amended 2026-11-13): the commit and proving part over the baseline's GPU-seconds per reply

session_generation_gpu_seconds_per_reply.$comment: CO-7 (amended 2026-11-13): the generation phase's GPU-seconds over N, mean of the counted sessions, scope whole_wall; null when the system has no generation phase of its own

session_generation_multiple.$comment: CO-7 (amended 2026-11-13): the session's generation part over the baseline's GPU-seconds per reply

session_gpu_seconds_per_reply.$comment: CO-1: GPU-seconds from the start of commit to the release of the last proof, over N; mean of the counted sessions

session_multiple.$comment: CO-5: session cost per reply over the baseline's GPU-seconds per reply, printed as 'whole sessions of N replies'

generation_gpu_seconds_per_reply.$comment: CO-3: the generation phase's GPU-seconds (between the adapter's generation marks) over the session's N replies, included in m; null when the session has no generation phase

further_reply.$comment: CO-9: this session's GPU-seconds from the start of prove to its last reply, over its replies

further_reply_generation.$comment: CO-9: this session's generation part per reply, from the AD-4 marks or the adapter's reported phase

one_time.$comment: CO-9: this session's one-time work in GPU-seconds (commit start to prove start, plus a reused setup's own and its restore)

steady_generation_gpu_seconds_per_reply.$comment: CO-7: the generation phase's part of m, mean of the counted sessions; null when the system has no generation phase of its own or no steady state

steady_gpu_seconds_per_reply.$comment: CO-3: mean m of the counted sessions; null when any counted session has no steady state

steady_proving_gpu_seconds_per_reply.$comment: CO-7: m less its generation part, mean of the counted sessions; null as the generation part

further_reply_gpu_seconds.$comment: CO-9 (Q55): the cost of a further reply, GPU-seconds held (bound GPUs x wall time) from the start of prove to the last reply, summed over the counted sessions and divided by their summed replies (pooled), scope prove.session; stats hold each session's own value (min, max, median) and n

further_reply_generation_gpu_seconds.$comment: CO-9: the further reply's generation part, pooled the same way: the AD-4 phase (D-L1-FURTHER-GENERATION) or, for a system with no phase of its own, the generation phase its adapter reports once each session's reported prove phases sum to its harness-timed prove call within the tolerance (D-L1-FURTHER-GENERATION-ADAPTER, labelled in its note); null (not_applicable) with no split

further_reply_proving_gpu_seconds.$comment: CO-9: the further reply less its generation part, everything a reply costs once its tokens exist; null with the generation part

further_reply_split.$comment: CO-9: where the generation part comes from, the same for every counted session or none (source null, with the cause); the adapter phases' sum against the prove call per session, and the tolerance

further_reply_multiple.$comment: CO-9: the further reply over the baseline's GPU-seconds per reply (D-L1-MULTIPLE), the total multiple the ladder prints; stats hold each session's own over the same baseline

further_reply_proving_multiple.$comment: CO-9: the further reply's proving part over the baseline's GPU-seconds per reply, the proving multiple the ladder prints; null with the split

further_reply_tokens_per_gpu_second.$comment: CO-8 (amended 2026-11-26, Q55): the request's reply tokens over the further reply, scope prove.session; the baseline's served rate over it is further_reply_multiple

further_reply_usd_per_reply.$comment: CO-9: the further reply at the release's price per GPU-hour (Cost only)

one_time_gpu_seconds.$comment: CO-9: the one-time work, never divided by N: per session the GPU-seconds from the start of commit to the start of prove, plus, for a session that reused a setup, the setup record's gpu_seconds and the restore of its state; mean over the counted sessions with range and n, unit gpu_s

one_time_usd.$comment: CO-9: the one-time work at the release's price per GPU-hour (Cost only)

one_time_mark_replies.$comment: CO-9: ceil(19 x one_time_gpu_seconds / further_reply_gpu_seconds), the fewest replies at which the one-time work is at most 5 % of the total, unit count

one_time_setups.$comment: CO-9: each setup the counted sessions reused, by its record, with its own GPU-seconds (setup/1 gpu_seconds)

proving_batch.$comment: CO-9: the replies one proof batch holds (the workload's shape.batch_size), which the proving part depends on

prove_gpu_util_mean.$comment: CO-9 (Q55, point 4): the prove step's sampled GPU utilisation (run.json metrics prove_gpu_util_mean, %), D-STAT over the counted sessions: a diagnostic under Cost, never a ladder figure

prove_gpu_memory_peak.$comment: CO-9 (Q55, point 4): the prove step's peak GPU memory (run.json metrics prove_gpu_memory_peak, MiB), D-STAT over the counted sessions: a diagnostic under Cost

runs.$comment: RFC-0018 FI-8, FI-9 (amended 2026-11-15): each fidelity run record of the rung, its part (null for fidelity-run.json), its engine and the slot count it stores

slots.$comment: FM-5 (amended 2026-11-15): the slot count of the rung's fidelity runs; null for a run part in vLLM, which sends every prompt in one generate call

teacher_forced.$comment: RFC-0018 SI-9: teacher-forced top-token agreement and KL (FI-10 to FI-15) from teacher-forced.json, printed beside fidelity; absent while not scored. No check, petal, position or order reads it

percent_interval.$comment: SI-9 (amended 2026-11-15): the 95 % bootstrap interval of percent over the prompts, [low, high], computed by the board (interval_rule); null for a failed entry

percent.$comment: SI-9 (amended 2026-11-14): mean ÷ positions × 100, the site's Fidelity; computed by the board

label.const: computed by the system's own code on the reference reply, not by the proved computation
computed by the system's own code on the reference reply, not by the proved computation

percent_interval.$comment: SI-9 (amended 2026-11-15): the 95 % bootstrap interval of percent over the prompts, [low, high], computed by the board (interval_rule); null for a failed entry

percent.$comment: SI-9 (amended 2026-11-14): mean ÷ positions × 100, the site's Fidelity; computed by the board

proved_tokens.$comment: FI-16: the positions at which a proof states the committed model's top token on the reference's text, and those where the row's pass gave it; null without a pass or without a proved reply for every prompt

scope_cell.$comment: one cell of Machine-checked's scope card, copied from properties/2; printed as a recorded fact, it sets no state

visible_item.$comment: Weights hidden: one value a proof leaves visible, copied from properties/2; only fitted_to_weights sets a state (WH-5)

baseline_sides.$comment: RFC-0018 CO-10 (proposed 2026-11-27, Q56): the serving baseline on each side of the request. The prompt side is the rung's request A (the level's prompts, a one-token reply) served on the level's ladder and taken by CO-4's rule (D-L1-BASELINE); the reply side is the rung's baseline less it (D-L1-BASELINE-REPLY, null with the cause when it is not larger); prompt_share is their ratio s_A / s_B. Present only on a board built by the cost of a further reply where a run of request A is stored; diagnostics, read by no position or check

row_sides.$comment: RFC-0018 CO-10 (proposed 2026-11-27, Q56): the row's further reply (CO-9) on the prompt side and on the reply side, each with its generation and proving part, pooled over the counted sessions; a part is the measured core the adapter reports (a phase's `__prompt` and `__reply` parts, source adapter) plus the rest apportioned by position (`positions`), and generation with no reported core is null with the cause. The multiples divide a prompt-side cost by the prompt side of the baseline and a reply-side cost by its reply side. Present only where the rung's baseline has `sides`; diagnostics, read by no position or check

description: releases/<release>/board.json, written by `iproofs release board` from stored records only (RFC-0018 §The board file). Rungs in the level file's order; rows in the order rule's order (OR-5).

cost_rule.$comment: RFC-0018 Q55, CO-9: present on a board built by the cost of a further reply (every release after v1.0); absent on a board built by the whole-session rule (CO-5 as Q29 amended it, v1.0)

date.$comment: the newest run date among the records read; null when nothing has run

frontier.$comment: OR-6: the largest rung with a passed row; null when no row has passed

title: Level board (RFC-0018 §The board file)

allOf.$comment: RFC-0018 Q55, CO-9: a board built by the cost of a further reply gives every row its CO-9 figures and every counted session its own
